title: Spherical Sampling Exploration: Reconstruction Accuracy of Classical and Polyhedral Sampling Schemes on the Sphere
description:
A set of Jupyter notebooks exploring sampling schemes on the sphere and the accuracy with which a bandlimited spherical function can be reconstructed from samples taken on each one.

The work covers the mathematical background of spherical harmonics and the spherical Fourier transform, then compares two families of grids: classical quadrature-based grids (Driscoll–Healy, Gauss–Legendre, McEwen–Wiaux) and polyhedral grids built by refining tetrahedral, octahedral and icosahedral meshes. For each scheme the notebooks measure reconstruction error against a known ground-truth signal, resolved per spherical harmonic mode and per degree, and examine the conditioning of the associated transforms.
